nodes.evidence: - **Plugin-source gates.** `plugin-source-gates.sh --staged | --range <base-ref> [<head-ref>] [--report <file>]` judges one candidate tree, the index (`--staged`) or `<head-ref>` (`--range`, path set from `merge-base(<base-ref>, <head-ref>)`), with skill-registry, native-contract, genericity and behavior-registry. **The judged branch never supplies its own judge:** the gate scripts, their checker code (`afk_judge_dir`) and the rule file `hooks/lib/sensitive-patterns.tsv` come from the runner's own plugin tree. At commit that is the installed plugin `precommit-gates.sh` runs from; in a pull request it is the fetched tip of the target branch, and the branch's own runner runs as well, so a gate the branch adds is exercised too. The candidate tree is data only: it is checked out of a private index into a temporary folder, so untracked files, unstaged edits and the pass cache never reach a verdict. A `.claude/hooks/.gate-disabled` in the candidate is data too: the runner sets `AFK_IGNORE_GATE_SENTINEL=1`, and its gates ignore the sentinel. Before any program starts, the runner drops relative, unreadable and in-repository folders from `PATH` with shell builtins only; the protected roots are the folder holding the nearest `.git`; an absolute `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR` and `GIT_DIR`; for that `.git` and for `GIT_DIR`, a gitfile's folder and its `gitdir:` target, the git directory's `commondir` (unless `GIT_COMMON_DIR` is set) and the `core.worktree` in its `config` or `config.worktree`; and the folder holding any of these that is named `.git`. A relative git variable, a gitfile, `commondir` or `core.worktree` it cannot read, or a start outside any repository without `GIT_WORK_TREE` is incomplete input. Every judge Python call runs `afk-python -I` from an absolute path outside the repository (compared by physical path: links and junctions resolved, letter case folded where the filesystem folds it), with `PYTHONPATH` and `PYTHONHOME` unset and repository directories dropped from `PATH`, so a candidate module such as `json.py` cannot shadow the checker; no such interpreter is incomplete input. Judge git calls run the absolute `git` found the same way (`AFK_JUDGE_GIT`), and the runner exports `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1` so Windows never starts a program from the candidate folder. The repository is the plugin when `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` names `afk` at the base revision or in the candidate; elsewhere the runner exits 0 and runs nothing. In the plugin, a candidate that deletes the manifest, the runner, `BEHAVIORS.md`, `skills/` or a gate script is incomplete input. **Parity is a fixture contract:** one change returns the same (gate, verdict, finding) tuples staged and in a pull request (`scripts/tests/test_plugin_source_gates.py`: deletion, rename, untracked-before-stage, allowed genericity, provider manifest, managed behavior, registry lockstep, crash, no-op gate, control-file deletions). Exit 0 passes; exit 2 is a block, a crash, a missing verdict, or input it could not build. `--report` writes `<gate>\t<verdict>\t<finding line>`, the temporary folder written as `<tree>`. **Relaxing a gate on purpose:** add the token or line to the allow file the gate names (`hooks/genericity-allow.txt`, `hooks/native-contract-allow.txt`); a change the target's gate still refuses needs the `afk-gate-override` label on the pull request, which turns the target pass into a warning while the branch's own gates still block, and a local `git commit --no-verify`. A target branch with no runner in its history leaves the branch's gates to judge alone. Who may apply the label is a repository-label decision: on an organization repository, Triage users can apply labels. CI's target pass runs from the pull request's own workflow file, so a pull request that edits `.github/workflows/` can drop it; a workflow diff needs human review. The full fix is a required workflow owned by the target branch, a repository setting for the owner.

Every judge Python call runs `afk-python -I` from an absolute path outside the repository (compared by physical path: links and junctions resolved, letter case folded where the filesystem folds it), with `PYTHONPATH` and `PYTHONHOME` unset and repository directories dropped from `PATH`, so a candidate module such as `json.py` cannot shadow the checker; no such interpreter is incomplete input. Judge git calls run the absolute `git` found the same way (`AFK_JUDGE_GIT`), and the runner exports `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1` so Windows never starts a program from the candidate folder. The repository is the plugin when `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` names `afk` at the base revision or in the candidate; elsewhere the runner exits 0 and runs nothing. In the plugin, a candidate that deletes the manifest, the runner, `BEHAVIORS.md`, `skills/` or a gate script is incomplete input. **Parity is a fixture contract:** one change returns the same (gate, verdict, finding) tuples staged and in a pull request (`scripts/tests/test_plugin_source_gates.py`: deletion, rename, untracked-before-stage, allowed genericity, provider manifest, managed behavior, registry lockstep, crash, no-op gate, control-file deletions). Exit 0 passes; exit 2 is a block, a crash, a missing verdict, or input it could not build. `--report` writes `<gate>\t<verdict>\t<finding line>`, the temporary folder written as `<tree>`. **Relaxing a gate on purpose:** add the token or line to the allow file the gate names (`hooks/genericity-allow.txt`, `hooks/native-contract-allow.txt`); a change the target's gate still refuses needs the `afk-gate-override` label on the pull request, which turns the target pass into a warning while the branch's own gates still block, and a local `git commit --no-verify`. A target branch with no runner in its history leaves the branch's gates to judge alone. Who may apply the label is a repository-label decision: on an organization repository, Triage users can apply labels. CI's target pass runs from the pull request's own workflow file, so a pull request that edits `.github/workflows/` can drop it; a workflow diff needs human review. The full fix is a required workflow owned by the target branch, a repository setting for the owner.

The init hold has no agent recovery: a new `.afk/` is a collapsed untracked folder, which the recovery puts in the human-only list, so the hold stays until `.afk/` leaves git status (committed or deleted) or the 24-hour sweep. Today the same hold arises only when the session itself sits in a main checkout.

Personal-file writes (set, and `KEY=` deletion for AC-024) land in <Y common dir>/afk/config.yaml, and install-git-hooks.sh writes Y's common hooks folder; git status lists neither, so no hold follows (lab D5, D6, B15).

AC-061 `git -C <Y> worktree remove <absolute path>` without --force, for a worktree of Y inside another repository Z, is allowed when the worktree is clean, unoccupied and on an unprotected branch, from any session folder (lab A5, C1, C6, C8). It is refused when the worktree has changes (C2), when another live session holds it (C3), when its branch is protected (C4), and with --force and no ignored files (C7). The session's own repository plays no part: the target's placement decides. The branch stays (C1). A locked worktree passes the guard and git exits 128 (C10).

The registered-basename form `git -C <Y> worktree remove <name>` is refused as 'this is the main checkout': the operand resolves to <Y>/<name>, which lies inside Y, so the `git worktree list` fallback never runs (lab C5). No test covers the fallback. The walk must pass the absolute worktree path.

When the session's own folder is Z's main checkout and Y's worktree is the only untracked content of a folder in Z (<Z>/wc/, or <Z>/.claude/worktrees/wa with nothing else under .claude/), the removal changes Z's git status: the meter holds Z and the next walk step in Z is refused (lab E1, E2, E5, E6). The worktree exemption counts only Z's own worktrees. Recovery is human-only. From another folder Z is never snapshotted (E4, D3); a folder that keeps other untracked files only compares its mtime and no hold follows (D1).

Writes under the home folder are allowed: the repository list, root creation with `mkdir -p`, the marker by redirect or Write, and a marker beside a linked worktree in <root>/<shortName>/ (lab A6-A9, A13), because placement finds no .git above. Catalog R-02 keeps the root outside every git repository, which matches.

After install-git-hooks.sh in Y, the backstop refuses an agent commit in Y's main checkout (lab C14) and passes an agent `git worktree remove` (lab C13). No walk step commits or moves a ref in Y: the scripts run only `git rev-parse` and `git config --get` (INV-007 REPORT.md), and AC-061 keeps the branch.

The M6 add/move placement check leaves remove unchanged only if it is gated on the operation kind: move and remove share one loop in decide() and one parser branch, and `git worktree add` is not parsed at all today. The remove path already runs git status and, on a branch, the forge lookup; those reads are not new.

SAFETY.md and its managed behavior line say an agent changes repository files only from a linked worktree its session or team owns. The walk writes Y's main checkout (`init`) and Y's shared state (personal file, git hooks) from outside any such worktree. The design rests on the guard not seeing script targets, not on a stated exception, so the rule text needs a setup exception, and the BEHAVIORS.md row change engages the behavior registry gate.

A change to a guard placement or verdict rule, or to the refusal text, updates SAFETY.md 'Worktree per session', its BEHAVIORS.md row, PROVIDERS.md 'Protected-branch guard', hooks/README.md, CAPABILITIES.md, nine guard test files and docs/afk/protected-branch-guard/PRD.md in the same commit.

'Idle' as the guard knows it is the absence of another live agent session's occupancy record; a human's own terminal or IDE in the worktree leaves no record, so the guard treats it as idle. The AC-061 'idle' test needs its own check or accepts this gap.

A guard refusal text names a worktree move and AFK_ALLOW_PROTECTED=1 as the way out; neither is the walk's recovery, so the new `failed` status should carry the walk's own reason and rerun command, not the guard's Move hint.
